# InferMaps: digit-only names always make a map; string-only classes need
# 50 properties; otherwise names must look random enough for the number of
# properties, and all values must be compatible (modulo null). The class
# attributes go to both the map and its values.
builder prov
prim i integer
prim d double
str s unrestricted
prim nul null
prim b bool
cls digits 1:i,22:s,333:b n=Digits
cls strs xqzv:s,kwjh:s,pfgt:s n=Strings
cls rnd xqzvw:i,kwjhq:i,pfgtz:i n=Random
cls eng name:i,age:i,city:i n=English
cls mixed xqzvw:i,kwjhq:s,pfgtz:i n=Mixed
union ni i,nul n=NullableInt
cls nulls xqzvw:i,kwjhq:ni,pfgtz:nul n=Nulls
cls nums xqzvw:i,kwjhq:d n=Numbers
cls one xqzvw:i n=One
ucls fixed fixed xqzvw:i,kwjhq:i n=Fixed
cls top d:digits,s:strs,r:rnd,e:eng,m:mixed,n:nulls,nu:nums,o:one,f:fixed n=Top
top Top top
finish printonrewrite
infermaps debug
infermaps
infermaps conflate
gc
print

# Classes inside classes: the outer map's values unify the inner classes.
builder
prim i integer
cls in1 a:i n=In1
cls in2 a:i n=In2
cls outer qxzv:in1,zzkq:in2,jjwx:in1 n=Outer
cls top o:outer n=Top
top Top top
finish
infermaps debug
print
